questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really like Canada as a country, the people are friendly and nice - had travelled here before - but hadn't been on the West Coast yet. Heard good things about Vancouver as a city and metropole with amazing opportunities in terms of exploring beautiful nature and outdoor activities. And then I chose UBC because of it's good reputation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was fairly straight forward. I must admit that I have a good friend who was also on abroad at UBC the semester before me, so I had some sort of a hotline connection to her, where I could ask her stuff I wasn't sure about, which helped me quite a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular really. But I'll also emphasize that going to Vancouver on exchange is probably one of the smallest culture shocks or changes one can experience, if deciding to study somewhere outside of EU. We had a intro-day at UBC, which provided information and a tour around Campus but besides that I figured things out myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me it was easy, because it was a fellow KU student who asked me if I wanted to live in an apartment together, so I spent close to no time looking for housing. Lucky me. She found it on Airbnb. A bit pricey, but the apartment was in Downtown Vancouver. And nice to live with other Danish students. We had a good time together! The level of easyness depend on one's budget of course. My tip is to think about exchange as an investment in 4 months thats going to be a memory of a livetime, so maybe increase your housing budget a little if possible of course. Because the time on exchange is worth it kinda.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's of course convenient to live on the Campus, but I liked living in Downtown Vancouver (30 min commute approx.), because I could do runs in Stanley Park, study at the good coffee spots in Gastown and just actually get the feeling of living in Vancouver. Don't think you do that if you live on campus, though it's probably a bit cheaper

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it's about 50% that get on-campus housing. That's of course not optimal, but just the conditions you know. Don't be sad about not getting on-campus housing, because all the good stuff happen off-campus anyway.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was step-by-step pretty straight forward. One step at a time, nothing complex. Just check KU-mail regularly and then everything is streamlined. The proces was transparent and made sense all the way through.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guess help was available if wanted. If something isn't done correctly in the process, then they people at UBC are good at writing to you about what needs to be corrected.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful. Got the courses I applied for. Didn't do the exchange for the courses though. I found something that sounded interesting. But fair to say it isn't perfectly related to my study at KU. But that's the beauty of going on exchange.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Use this site, and make sure that the courses you apply for correlate with the Faculty that you are enrolled in:
https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/course-descriptions/courses-facultyschoolcollege

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy to be fair. I bit difficult because I'm not used to delve into e.g. anthropological academics, but it's also 200-level courses which maybe explains the level. I think it was okay. Wasn't here in Vancouver to drown in school stuff :) But the courses were interesting and learned a lot from them!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Pretty much the same, but slightly more weekly submissions, lecture notes and stuff like that to make sure that you are following along the pensum.
Some courses do attendance. Either explicitly or implicitly by having in-class activities you have to submit, and you can only do them if you are there physically.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ANTH_V 217 001 Culture and Communication
ENST_V 211 101 The State of the Earth
SOCI_V 260 101 Work and Society
SOCI_V 280 101 Data and Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ENST_V 211 101 The State of the Earth: It's like geography, but in an interesting way.
SOCI_V 260 101 Work and Society: Learned about work and how that has changed through history and also varies between countries and that.
SOCI_V 280 101 Data and Society: A lot about AI and automation which is somewhat diffuse, but relevant to learn about it

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I will just say that's extremely difficult to budget an exchange, and some months where expensive because of weekend trips basically every weekend. Bank account is bleeding, but social and cultural capital is levelling up (Bourdieu).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are less expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts. So many clubs. Some would say too many.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The VOC (Varsity Outdoor Club). I did some hikes with them. They were amazing and meet people through that activity that I eventually did weekend trips with on own hand.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Everything :) No for real, get outside. Nature stuff like the following.
Garibaldi, Panorama Ridge, Joffre Lakes, Cypress, Grouse and Crown Mountain. 
Vancouver Island: Tofino, Ucluelet, 5040 Peak, Campbell River, Sooke, Victoria
Banff: Sentinel Pass, Moraine Lake, Plain of Six Glaciers, Johnston Canyon
Go to Seattle, Olympic and Mt Rainier National Park

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: In every class, see if you can find someone to talk with. They are all friendly and interested in you and your life back home.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
None.
Took me a week to accept the premise of tipping 15-20% at restaurants and places like that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open and talkative Canadians are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Life here is expensive, but not as expensive as in CPH. Only more expensive because you do more stuff than back home.

Bring some Gore-Tex. It rains quite a lot, but on Sunny days, Vancouver is amazingggg. So get here early (a few weeks before school starts maybe) to enjoy the weather in August, if starting september.

Canada is multicultural. It's fascinating to hear stories and origins of fellow students, and make sure to spend some time getting to understand Vancouver, the Indigenous people. It's interesting.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you don't get housing on-campus, then Downtown Vancouver is maybe not the perfection option to go with. I really liked it, but if I had to choose a place to live now that I have been here for some amount of time, I'd say either Kitsilano or Mt. Pleasant are good options as well. Though Downtown is also nice, but maybe a bit to central. Like living in K in Copenhagen or sum'tin.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The hikes and trips with people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To accept the fact that it's not possible to do everything you want to do. We have 24 hours a day, and need time to recharge sometimes. Be proactive and do stuff, but also chill and enjoy the fact that you live abroad and life is good, no matter if you do many things or not.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Yolo

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
